origin.notes: Tactical motifs are descriptive pattern names of long and mostly anonymous usage. The Chess Informant classification is cited as a standard enumeration, not as the origin of the term.

definition_short: A line piece acts through another piece — attacking or defending beyond it.
definition_long:
A bishop, rook or queen exerts influence through an intervening unit. Two distinct uses share the name, and Chess Tempo maintains them as separate tags:

X-RAY ATTACK — the line piece attacks a target through an intervening piece, so the attack becomes real the moment the blocker leaves.
X-RAY DEFENCE — the line piece defends a friendly unit through an intervening piece, so a capture on that square is answered by a recapture that was not visible.

Sources also disagree about whether x-ray is distinct from pin and skewer at all; some treat all three as one family of line effects. This record keeps x-ray for the case where the effect operates THROUGH a piece without compelling it to move, which is what distinguishes it from a pin or skewer.
epistemic_note: Motif (D). Terminology genuinely contested: some sources fold x-ray into pin/skewer. The boundary chosen here is stated explicitly rather than presented as settled.

preconditions: A line piece, an intervening unit, and a further square of interest are collinear
indicators_for: The defence or attack becomes live as soon as the blocker moves
A capture on the far square is met by a recapture along the x-ray line
indicators_against: A second blocker sits further along the line

exceptions: An x-ray defence is illusory if the defending piece is itself pinned.
limitations: The pin/skewer/x-ray boundary is not agreed between sources; an explanation should prefer the more specific term when the position warrants it.

explanation_templates.beginner: This piece is working right through another piece — the moment the piece in the middle moves, the attack is real.
explanation_templates.intermediate: An x-ray: the {piece} defends {square} through {blocker}, so the recapture is available.
explanation_templates.advanced: X-ray. Prefer 'pin' or 'skewer' where the front piece is compelled; reserve x-ray for through-effects that compel nothing.
explanation_templates.hedge: Sources differ on where x-ray ends and pin or skewer begins.
